answer: Require each agent to lock a refundable stake tied to its transaction volume, like water slowly shaping a dune: making thousands of fake identities is expensive because every identity must fund its own stake, while honest agents recover theirs. A public reputation ledger acts as a crystal record of past behavior that cannot be rewritten, so a new fake identity starts with zero trust and cannot instantly access high-value work. Like an ocean diluting a drop, verification spreads across independent attestors, so an attacker cannot flood the system without paying on every front.
